findings.body:
**The `git` helper passes an `env` without `PATH`.**

`src/ops/review/internal/localReview.ts:24-29` sets `options.env` and does not include `PATH`. Node then looks up `git` on a default search path, normally `/usr/bin:/bin`, and not on the caller's `PATH`. Hosts with `git` elsewhere will fail with `ENOENT`. Examples are Nix, Homebrew on Linux, and custom toolchains.

Every caller is affected: `headMessage` and `evidenceRoot` here, and any other op that imports `git`. `headMessage` also hides the failure. It reports "current HEAD is unavailable" and does not surface the real cause.

Forward `PATH` from the parent process. Keep the other hardening variables.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
       env: {
+        PATH: process.env.PATH ?? '',
         GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1',
         GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: '/dev/null',
```
</details>
findings.title: The `git` helper passes an `env` without `PATH`.

findings.body:
**`canonicalReview` throws a `TypeError` when a value is `undefined`.**

`JSON.stringify(undefined)` returns `undefined`, so `.replace` at line 320 throws. This is reachable from the object branch at line 316. `Object.entries` keeps keys whose value is explicitly `undefined`, for example `{ principal: undefined }`. Zod keeps such keys when the input contains them. The same applies to functions and symbols.

`JSON.stringify` on the same object would drop the key. `reviewDigest` must be deterministic and must mirror the contract, so it should not crash on this input. Skip `undefined` entries in objects. Do this before sorting.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
       Object.entries(value)
+        .filter(([, val]) => val !== undefined)
         .sort(([a], [b]) => (a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0))
```
</details>
findings.title: `canonicalReview` throws a `TypeError` when a value is `undefined`.
